A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Advisor Models. All 15 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support matching the methods, experiments, equations and displays despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original advisor-training experiments on personalization, translation, tax reasoning and mathematics, together with transfer and capability-retention evaluations.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments on the retained tasks and adds software-agent efficiency, broader frontier-model transfer, scalability and direct-RL comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 adds an implemented multi-turn advising architecture that receives student actions and observations and supplies further advice, every five student actions in the SWE experiment. It also describes a tested advisor-as-tool-call variant (Section 3; Appendix B.2). V1's two-step and three-step pipelines and GRPO training remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds SWE Agent Efficiency using SWE-smith issues from the Tenacity repository, introducing multi-turn software repair with interaction-efficiency requirements. The original review-personalization, math-solutions, translation, tax and math-correctness tasks remain, although their presentation changes.

E2.justification: V2 adds PAG and an in-context preference oracle to personalization, explicitly separates student-only and untrained-advisor controls, and adds GEPA to the MTOB and RuleArena comparisons. It also evaluates direct student RL on MTOB and an efficiency-prompt control for SWE. GEPA is explicitly not evaluated on SWE (Sections 4.1, 4.3 and 4.4.3).

E3.justification: V2 introduces SWE issue filtering, a 40-interaction cap, and resolve-rate/step-count evaluation. Appendix A replaces v1's generic 10-epoch setting with domain-specific budgets, including 20 for MTOB and 40 for RuleArena; weak-initialization training changes from 30 to 20 epochs. Frontier-student configurations, Llama advisors, the 3B/7B direct-RL comparison and 100-user scaling also add experimental settings. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing rerun history.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of advisor-family dependence, scaling personalization to 100 users, performance relative to direct RL, and SWE advice before versus after training. Cross-family transfer analysis expands beyond review length (Appendices D–E). The initialization analysis is revised, while v1's qualitative reasoning-trace analysis of over-advising is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals, but v2 supplies them for reasoning comparisons previously presented as point estimates in v1 Table 1. V2 also introduces explicit p-values for GPT-5 MTOB and SWE transfer results. Evaluation run counts, seeds and the construction of the intervals/tests remain unspecified.

E6.justification: The three personalization advisor rewards change from 0.932/1.000/0.946 in v1 Figure 3 to 0.941/0.996/0.948 in v2 Figure 5. Reasoning, transfer and retention scores also change, and substantial SWE, frontier, Llama, scalability and direct-RL results are added. For example, v2 Figure 4 reports Gemini 3 Pro steps decreasing from 31.7 to 26.3. Revised budgets and model configurations prevent treating all cross-version score changes as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: V2 Appendix C.1 introduces a mathematical definition of the SWE reward: zero for unresolved issues and 0.5 + 0.5(40 − steps)/40 for resolved issues. The existing review-length reward is unchanged and relocated to Appendix C.2. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 makes low-cost training followed by frontier-model improvement a central contribution, adding explicit GPT-5 tax and Gemini software-agent efficiency claims to the abstract and conclusion. V1's parametric-memory framing is dropped. Its claim of transfer with no performance loss becomes a claim that useful gains survive transfer.

C2.justification: V1's explanation and mitigation discussion of over-advising—advisors solving problems that students copy—is removed. V2 instead develops interpretations involving harmful untrained advice, limited knowledge headroom, student-specific transfer losses and advantages over the preference oracle. It also reports that optional advisor queries fail because students rarely request help, and interprets limited math gains as knowledge saturation.

D1.justification: V2 adds SWE-specific hyperparameters, per-domain epoch tables, Tenacity data-selection instructions, interaction limits and scaled-personalization sampling details (Appendices A–D). SkyRL, the eight-H100 hardware disclosure and the code link are retained. Some specificity is lost: the math-correctness experiment no longer explicitly identifies v1's 1,000-example Omni-Math training set.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the parameter-efficient-finetuning discussion with substantive comparisons to trained prompt generators: Black-Box Prompt Optimization, PRewrite, Directional Stimulus Prompting and Matryoshka Pilot. V2 distinguishes expert supervision, static versus instance-specific outputs and output constraints. It also adds literature supporting personalization baselines, agent tasks and curriculum filtering.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The RQ-based evaluation narrative becomes a sequence covering specialized reasoning, frontier transfer, personalization and ablations. Related work and the appendices are reorganized, while retained review examples and prompts move to Appendices E.2 and F. The author list also changes.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. The framework diagram is redrawn, the introductory review example is replaced by a multi-turn training/transfer diagram, and the reasoning table becomes expanded plots. Initialization plots are merged, new ablation figures appear, and training settings are reorganized into hyperparameter and epoch tables.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's limited controls and evidence for frontier applicability through separate student/untrained-advisor comparisons, PAG/oracle and direct-RL comparisons, and frontier/multi-turn evaluations. Scalability and advisor-family ablations, closer prior-work comparisons and expanded training details further improve support and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed over-advising discussion and reporting errors, notably the abstract's claimed 24.6% Gemini 3 Pro step reduction versus Figure 4's 31.7-to-26.3 reduction, approximately 17%.
